brief: New fact: Octave could draw a QR on the TV and finish an OIDC device-authorization grant, approved on another device through the household's provider. Four questions: does this lift D-082's rejection; what the server would provide; how it sits beside Quick Connect; JS-039's priority and criteria.
tradeoff: Given up by viewers: a QR on Octave's sign-in screen, until Octave's project commits to drawing one. Nobody is locked out, since a provider account already reaches Octave by Quick Connect's code (D-082). Given up for good: a standard device grant any generic OIDC client could call, because no such client plays films here. Unverified: whether jellyfin-web's approval page takes a code from its address; which households' providers offer the grant; how many Octave users sit at a TV (PRODUCT.md calls it a desktop client).
entry: D-082 stands, and the grant is rejected as a second protocol, not deferred. 'Could' is not use, and no jellyscale work goes in for Octave (D-027). If a QR comes, it carries Quick Connect's own code in a link: one code, one expiry, one guessing bound, one approval, one ordinary token. A grant at jellyscale would be a second pending-code machine for the same outcome. A grant at the provider would make a provider token a credential, work only where the provider offers it, and move approval to where jellyscale cannot name the device. D-082's trigger is corrected, because 'ships the grant' can never fire for something that needs the server first. BL-229 is promoted when the project of a client that authorizes every media request states in an issue that it will draw the QR. It then becomes its own task directly after JS-039 (after JS-037 if JS-039 is not built), never a criterion of either. Product terms on promotion: the link opens the approval with the code filled in; a signed-out device signs in by password or provider and returns to the approval; the page names the device and app, and approves only on an explicit confirmation, never on opening; a page jellyscale serves lives under /jellyscale/v1/, documented. The TV shows one code, with a QR of the same code where the client draws one, never two flows. JS-039 keeps priority 36, its dependencies and its eight criteria. The grant itself reopens on a supported client that cannot speak Quick Connect, or an operator report of a provider policy that requires the provider's own device page.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'A password, a code entered on the TV from a phone, or the household's own single sign-on'; 'Octave first... (no jellyscale work goes in for it)'; 'what jellyscale adds beyond Jellyfin's API is something it can use, never something it needs'; 'Signing in is easy and safe'. Owner, 2026-11-22: nothing outruns the product.
